note: Tier 1 emission factors and scaling factors for rice methane, fertiliser N2O and urea CO2, plus AWD water-saving evidence. Used by server/services/carbon.ts and water-footprint.ts. Author: Nitya Prakash Pandey. Compiled 2026-09-29.

sources.ipcc2019_ch5: IPCC (2019) 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Vol. 4 (AFOLU), Ch. 5 Cropland, §5.5 Methane emissions from rice cultivation — Eq. 5.1-5.3, Tables 5.11-5.14. https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2019rf/vol4.html
sources.ipcc2019_ch11: IPCC (2019) 2019 Refinement, Vol. 4, Ch. 11 N2O emissions from managed soils and CO2 emissions from lime and urea application — Eq. 11.1, 11.9-11.10, 11.13; Table 11.1 and 11.3.
sources.ar6: IPCC AR6 WG1 (2021) Ch. 7, Table 7.15: GWP-100 CH4 (non-fossil origin) 27.0 ± 11, CH4 (fossil) 29.8 ± 11, N2O 273 ± 130.
sources.awd_water: Carrijo, Lundy & Linquist (2017) Rice yields and water use under alternate wetting and drying irrigation: a meta-analysis. Field Crops Research 203:173-180 — AWD cut water use 25.7 % on average; 'safe/mild' AWD (≥ −20 kPa) had no significant yield penalty. Lampayan et al. (2015) Field Crops Research 170:95-108 — 15-30 % water savings in Bangladesh, Philippines and Viet Nam.
sources.verra: Verra VM0051 Improved Management in Rice Production Systems v1.0 (2023). Figures here are an indicative Tier 1 estimate, NOT a VM0051 quantification: a verified project needs a validated baseline, monitoring (e.g. field water tubes / remote sensing), uncertainty deductions, leakage and third-party verification.
sources.water_benchmark: Mekonnen & Hoekstra (2011) The green, blue and grey water footprint of crops and derived crop products. HESS 15:1577-1600 — paddy rice global average 1,673 m³/t (green 1,146 · blue 341 · grey 187).

efBaseline.table: Table 5.11 (continuously flooded, no organic amendment, global default)

sfw._table: Table 5.12 — scaling factor for the water regime during the cultivation period (aggregated case)

sfp._table: Table 5.13 — scaling factor for the water regime before the cultivation period

cfoa._table: Table 5.14 — conversion factor for organic amendment (SFo = (1 + Σ ROAi·CFOAi)^0.59; ROA in t dry weight/ha for straw, t fresh weight/ha otherwise)

ef1Aggregated.table: Table 11.1 EF1 (aggregated, kg N2O-N per kg N)

ef1RiceByRegime.table: Table 11.1 EF1FR disaggregated: continuous flooding 0.003; single and multiple drainage 0.005

urea.note: IPCC Eq. 11.13 — assumes all synthetic N is applied as urea (46 % N), the dominant N source for smallholder rice in S/SE Asia

nRateKgHa._note: Typical recommended/observed mineral N per season, rounded — replace with farm records (per-asset override). Sources: BRRI Adhunik Dhaner Chash (Aman ≈ 70-90 kg N/ha); OUAT/Odisha package of practices kharif rice 60-80; Mekong rice 90-110 (IRRI/CLRRI surveys); PhilRice PalayCheck ≈ 80-90; Java 100-130 (BPS/IRRI). Non-rice crops: typical recommended rates (assumed).

croppingIntensity._note: Rice seasons per year assumed for annualising (per-asset override). Irrigated land in the Mekong grows 2-3 crops; rain-fed Aman/kharif land is mostly single-cropped rice.

awd.eligibility: AWD needs water control: irrigated (canal / tube-well / pump) fields that are flooded through the season. Rain-fed and deep-water rice cannot be drained on demand, so they are not eligible.

creditPrice.note: Indicative voluntary-market price range for agricultural methane reduction credits, USD per t CO2e
